title: Mixed and degeneracy identities on comonad powers
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an ordinary category and $T:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ an endofunctor, with powers $T^0=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$ and $T^{n+1}=T\circ T^n$ [def-trf-endofunctor-powers]. Write $1_a$ for the identity transformation of $T^a$, including $1_0$ on the identity functor, and $\star$ for horizontal composition: for $\alpha:F\to F\prime$ and $\beta:G\to G\prime$, $(\alpha\star\beta)_x=\alpha_{G\prime x}\circ F(\beta_x)$. Given a natural transformation $e:T\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$, set $B_n=T^{n+1}$ for $n\geq0$ and $d_i^n=1_i\star e\star1_{n-i}:B_n\to B_{n-1}$ for $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$. Let $c:T\to T^2$ be a natural transformation with $(e\star1_1)\circ c=1_1=(1_1\star e)\circ c$ and $(c\star1_1)\circ c=(1_1\star c)\circ c$. Set $s_i^n=1_i\star c\star1_{n-i}:B_n\to B_{n+1}$ for $n\geq0$ and $0\leq i\leq n$. These are natural transformations. For $n\geq2$ and $0\leq i<j\leq n-1$, $d_i^n\circ s_j^{n-1}=s_{j-1}^{n-2}\circ d_i^{n-1}$; for $n\geq2$ and $0\leq j< i-1\leq n-1$, $d_i^n\circ s_j^{n-1}=s_j^{n-2}\circ d_{i-1}^{n-1}$. For $n\geq1$ and $0\leq j\leq n-1$, $d_j^n\circ s_j^{n-1}=1_{B_{n-1}}=d_{j+1}^n\circ s_j^{n-1}$. For $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq j\leq n-1$, $s_i^n\circ s_j^{n-1}=s_{j+1}^n\circ s_i^{n-1}$. These assertions concern the displayed transformations themselves; no simplicial object is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, proof of conditions (1)(b)--(e), with Example 0G5M, example-godement.

proof.text: Use the powers of [def-trf-endofunctor-powers]. Their recursion gives $T^aT^b=T^{a+b}$: the case $a=0$ is the identity functor, and $T^{a+1}T^b=T(T^aT^b)=TT^{a+b}=T^{a+b+1}$ is the induction step. Use these identifications throughout. The displayed operators have components $(d_i^n)_x=T^i(e_{T^{n-i}x})$ and $(s_i^n)_x=T^i(c_{T^{n-i}x})$. For $f:x\to y$, naturality of $e$ at $T^{n-i}(f)$, followed by $T^i$, gives $T^n(f)(d_i^n)_x=(d_i^n)_yT^{n+1}(f)$; the same calculation with $c$ gives $T^{n+2}(f)(s_i^n)_x=(s_i^n)_yT^{n+1}(f)$. Thus both families are natural transformations with the stated sources and targets.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, proof of (1)(b)--(e); Example 0G5M, example-godement. Calculation 1.

proof.text: Suppose $n\ge2$ and $i<j\le n-1$. Put $k=j-i-1$ and $r=n-j-1$, both nonnegative. Remove the common outer whiskering $T^i$ and evaluate at $T^r x$. The two composites in the first mixed identity become $(e\star1_{k+2})\circ(1_{k+1}\star c)$ and $(1_k\star c)\circ(e\star1_{k+1})$. Apply [lem-amb-natural-transformation-whisker-exchange] with $\eta=1_k\star c:T^{k+1}\to T^{k+2}$ and $\theta=e:T\to\mathrm{id}$. Its two sides are exactly these composites. By the component definition of $\star$, both equal $e\star1_k\star c$. Restoring the outer and inner powers gives $d_i^n\circ s_j^{n-1}=1_i\star e\star1_k\star c\star1_r=s_{j-1}^{n-2}\circ d_i^{n-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, proof of (1)(b)--(e); Example 0G5M, example-godement. Calculation 2.

proof.text: Suppose $n\ge2$ and $0\le j<i-1\le n-1$. Put $k=i-j-2$ and $r=n-i$. Removing the outer $T^j$ and evaluating at $T^r x$, the composites become $(1_{k+2}\star e)\circ(c\star1_{k+1})$ and $(c\star1_k)\circ(1_{k+1}\star e)$. Apply [lem-amb-natural-transformation-whisker-exchange] with $\eta=1_k\star e:T^{k+1}\to T^k$ and $\theta=c:T\to T^2$. It equates precisely these two expressions, whose horizontal composite is $c\star1_k\star e$. Restoring the two powers gives $d_i^n\circ s_j^{n-1}=1_j\star c\star1_k\star e\star1_r=s_j^{n-2}\circ d_{i-1}^{n-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, proof of (1)(b)--(e); Example 0G5M, example-godement. Calculation 3.

proof.text: For $n\ge1$ and $0\le j\le n-1$, set $r=n-1-j$. Expanding components and using preservation of composition by $T^j$ gives $d_j^n\circ s_j^{n-1}=1_j\star((e\star1_1)\circ c)\star1_r$ and $d_{j+1}^n\circ s_j^{n-1}=1_j\star((1_1\star e)\circ c)\star1_r$. The two counit equations assumed in the statement replace each middle expression by $1_1$. Preservation of identities makes both results $1_{j+1+r}=1_n=1_{B_{n-1}}$.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, proof of (1)(b)--(e); Example 0G5M, example-godement. Calculation 4.

proof.text: For the degeneracy identity with $i<j\le n-1$, set $k=j-i-1$ and $r=n-j-1$. After removing $T^i$ and evaluating at $T^r x$, its left and right sides are $(c\star1_{k+2})\circ(1_{k+1}\star c)$ and $(1_{k+2}\star c)\circ(c\star1_{k+1})$. Apply [lem-amb-natural-transformation-whisker-exchange] with $\eta=1_k\star c:T^{k+1}\to T^{k+2}$ and $\theta=c:T\to T^2$. The equality it gives has these two sides, both equal to $c\star1_k\star c$ by the definition of horizontal composition. Restoring powers yields $s_i^n\circ s_j^{n-1}=1_i\star c\star1_k\star c\star1_r=s_{j+1}^n\circ s_i^{n-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, proof of (1)(b)--(e); Example 0G5M, example-godement. Calculation 5.

proof.text: For the remaining degeneracy case $i=j$, set $r=n-1-i$. Component expansion gives $s_i^n\circ s_i^{n-1}=1_i\star((c\star1_1)\circ c)\star1_r$ and $s_{i+1}^n\circ s_i^{n-1}=1_i\star((1_1\star c)\circ c)\star1_r$. These are equal by the assumed coassociativity equation, evaluated at $T^r x$ and then mapped by $T^i$. Together with the preceding case this proves the identity for every $0\le i\le j\le n-1$, including $n=1,i=j=0$.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, proof of (1)(b)--(e); Example 0G5M, example-godement. Calculation 6.
